clue.text: Lords and ladies crazed by drink

parts.note: cuckoo is informal for mad
a pint is a glass of beer

explanation.surface: Members of the aristocracy have been driven wild by alcohol at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' looks like nobility, but it is the country name of a wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and ladies is a folk name for the wild arum, a woodland plant also called the cuckoo pint.

clue.text: Rhino getting caught on tree

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the ash is a tree
in a down clue, on means placed above

explanation.surface: A rhinoceros gets snagged on a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhino' is old British slang for money, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is dated British slang for money, so it can stand for cash.

clue.text: Composite picture showing island over a period

parts.note: Coll is an island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland
an age is a period of time
in a down clue, over means placed above

explanation.surface: A montage depicts an island across a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is an artwork assembled from assorted pieces stuck together, a composite image.

clue.text: Running wild, start to hack into rotten pomegranate

indicators.note: one piece is put into another, sitting inside it
something rotten has decayed out of shape, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of hack

explanation.surface: Someone goes berserk and starts hacking at a mouldy pomegranate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the rampage is to rush about violently and uncontrollably, the idiom for running wild.

clue.text: Quiet, relaxed sound reproduction

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
lay back, the past of lie back, means relaxed

explanation.surface: Soft, mellow audio is played through the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Playback is the replaying of recorded sound or video, reproducing what was recorded.

clue.text: Slender point on missile

parts.note: north is a compass point
an arrow is a missile shot from a bow
in a down clue, on means placed above

explanation.surface: The thin, sharp tip on a projectile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' looks like the tip of the missile; it is a compass direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means of small width, thin, which is what slender describes.

clue.text: Long way away, in the middle of hunting trip

indicators.note: only the central part of the phrase that follows is kept, its ends trimmed off

parts.note: a safari is a hunting trip; drop its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone on a hunting expedition finds themselves far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at a great distance, so it replaces the phrase meaning a long way off.

clue.text: Fellow not just found in amusements

parts.note: F is short for fellow
unfair means not just

explanation.surface: A man finds himself treated unjustly at an arcade.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair is a travelling show of rides and stalls, a collection of amusements.

clue.text: Needy girls worked without protest

indicators.note: worked means shaped or manipulated, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor young women laboured without complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To act resignedly is to accept something unwelcome without complaining or resisting.

clue.text: Problem with locks for carp

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: hair that has divided at the ends
second meaning: to quibble over trivial distinctions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, and 'locks' like canal gates; here locks are hair and carp is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily, and the idiom for making overly fine distinctions is the same phrase.

clue.text: Responsibility of running large country

parts.note: a machine that is running is on
the United States

explanation.surface: The burden that falls on whoever governs a big nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a duty or burden placed on someone, a near synonym for responsibility.

clue.text: London borough's accepting minimal cash payment for services for state

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Newham is a borough in east London, plus the S of the possessive
a penny, the smallest coin
hire is the fee for someone's work

explanation.surface: A London council accepts a tiny fee for the services it provides.
explanation.definitionFit: New Hampshire is one of the fifty states of the USA, in New England.

clue.text: A lot of water to satisfy thirst, say? Not at first

indicators.note: the opening letter is not there, so the word starts one place later

parts.note: to slake is to quench thirst

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether gulping vast quantities of water would quench their thirst.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is a large body of standing water, so 'a lot of water' describes one loosely.

clue.text: Recoil, and express dissatisfaction with cake verbally

parts.note: to boo is to jeer

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the word for the cake counts by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a meringue is a sweet baked from egg white

explanation.surface: Someone flinches and complains out loud about a disappointing cake.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to boomerang is to backfire on the one who started it, as a thrown boomerang comes back.

clue.text: Pompous officer shows face, a month on beat

parts.note: pan is slang for face
Jan is short for January
to drum is to beat
in a down clue, on means placed above

explanation.surface: A self-important policeman shows his face after a month on the beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' suggests a policeman's patrol; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A panjandrum is a self-important official who acts with great pretension, a pompous dignitary.

clue.text: Suspension of a governor by an ecclesiastical organisation

parts.note: taken as written
a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor
taken as written
CE is the Church of England
by means next to, joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A colonial governor is suspended from office by a church body.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension, as when a rule or title is held in abeyance.

clue.text: Order fish, and get with tail removed

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its end, so its final letter goes

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
taken as written

explanation.surface: At a restaurant, someone orders fish and receives it without its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like asking for food; it is a command.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a task is to order or instruct them to do it.

clue.text: Cheer up! The worst is over. Xanthippe

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: rah is a cheer

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word runs the other way

parts.note: the nadir is the lowest point

explanation.surface: A comforting remark that the bad times have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as reassurance; Xanthippe, wife of Socrates, was famous as a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthippe, Socrates' wife, became a byword for a bad-tempered, nagging woman, exactly a harridan.

clue.text: Flier consuming chop and banger

indicators.note: something consuming another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a jay is a bird
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A bird eats a pork chop and a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang both for a sausage and for a clapped-out old car; the chop-and-banger surface plays on the food sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is a decrepit old motor car, which British slang also calls an old banger.

clue.text: The party's over — Henry ejected the little bounder

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the words are read backwards
something ejected is thrown out, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written
a revel is a lively celebration
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance; this letter is thrown out

explanation.surface: A party ends badly when Henry is thrown out by the bouncer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad, but here it is literally something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a young hare, and a hare is an animal that bounds, so the little bounder fits.

clue.text: Scots head may have this soothing influence before exam

parts.note: balm soothes
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A Scottish headteacher might need calming before the exams begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots head' suggests a head teacher, but it is a head wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a flat Scottish brimless cap, so it is something a head in Scotland may wear.

clue.text: Favour mechanical repetition incorporating routine

indicators.note: incorporating means taking into its body, so one word holds another

parts.note: learning by rote is learning by mechanical repetition
a set is a fixed routine, as in a set procedure

explanation.surface: Someone prefers learning by drill, built into a daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a verb meaning prefer; it is a noun, a ribbon badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or rosette worn as a badge of support, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Make great effort in race

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exert oneself to the limit
second meaning: a breed or line of descent

explanation.surface: A runner pushes hard during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a running contest; here it means a breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for exerting oneself and as a noun for a breed or variety of animal or plant.

clue.text: Person setting course around midnight is new pilot

parts.note: N is short for new

indicators.note: one piece goes around another, holding it inside

parts.note: an aviator flies a plane
read literally, the middle of the word night is its central letter

explanation.surface: A newly qualified pilot plots a flight path late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator plans and directs the route of a ship or aircraft, setting its course.

clue.text: Band of men who fight hard

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A troop of soldiers who fight fiercely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band of men' looks like a group of people; the band is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of fabric worn over the shoulder or round the waist, a band.

clue.text: Christopher receives new contract

indicators.note: something that receives takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher
N is short for new

explanation.surface: A man named Christopher is handed a fresh deal to sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, an agreement; it is the verb, as in knitting one's brows.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit the brows is to draw them together in a frown, so knit can mean to contract.

clue.text: Sort of ferry McGregor's leaving by, separately

indicators.note: letters that leave a word are taken out of it
separately says the departing pair go one at a time, from different places

parts.note: Rob Roy MacGregor was the Scottish outlaw hero
taken as written; these two letters depart, one from each half

explanation.surface: A man named McGregor walks off a ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' says the two letters go one at a time, each from a different word of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry that vehicles drive straight on and off.

clue.text: When cooked the ant bird is tough

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird that eats ants turns out leathery when roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hard-bitten has been toughened by experience and is unsentimental, hence tough.

clue.text: China tea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang, china plate for a friend
second meaning: a South American herbal infusion

explanation.walkthrough: 'China tea' reads as one drink. Cockney rhyming slang shortens 'china plate' to china, meaning pal; the tea is maté, brewed from yerba leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate means a pal, which rhyming slang calls china, and also names the yerba infusion drunk in Argentina.

clue.text: Whatever happens, innate envy will come out

indicators.note: coming out suggests emerging in a different form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Jealousy that is inborn will surface sooner or later, come what may.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means regardless of circumstances, the same as come what may.
